scope: exploratory direct-measurement screen on seven taxa with harmonized comparative capitulum-width and phyllary-protrusion measurements

capitulum_width_by_orientation.interpretation: No evidence that the directly measured capitulum-width component is obligatorily coupled to erect versus nodding state in this seven-taxon panel.

phyllary_protrusion_by_orientation.interpretation: Nodding taxa have smaller phyllary protrusion in this restricted panel, but the association is borderline and strongly vulnerable to clade/sample composition.

phyllary_protrusion_by_capitulum_width.interpretation: Direct display width and phyllary protrusion are not detectably coupled after Brownian phylogenetic correction in this restricted panel.

hypothesis_consequence: The direct measurements do not support a single obligatory display-orientation-defence axis. They justify testing module-specific transition histories against the common-lability alternative once Japan38/expanded topology and broader direct trait coverage are available.
claim_boundary: Seven taxa are insufficient for a general adaptive or convergence claim. Taxa are clustered by lineage and source study, so these values are a diagnostic only. Do not interpret the phyllary-orientation result as defensive adaptation.
